data.title: KSrelief Supports Distribution of 500,000 Mosquito Nets to Protect One Million Displaced Persons in Yemen
data.content:
Aden, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) supported a campaign to distribute mosquito nets and implement field health interventions, including screening and treatment for malaria and dengue fever, as well as entomological surveys in displacement camps, as part of the malaria control project in Yemen. This campaign is in cooperation with the World Health Organization (WHO) and the National Malaria and Vector-Borne Disease Control Program.
    The campaign, launched yesterday, aims to distribute 500,000 mosquito nets to approximately one million displaced persons in more than 629 camps across several governorates in Yemen to reduce the spread of vector-borne diseases and strengthen health prevention measures. Approximately 25,000 mosquito nets have been allocated to Aden Governorate, with priority given to Al-Firdous Camp and newly established displacement camps. Field teams are expected to cover all camps in Aden within a week before moving to other governorates.
    Director General of the National Malaria and Vector-Borne Disease Control Program Dr. Yasser Abdullah Bahashim explained that the KSrelief-supported campaign goes beyond distributing mosquito nets to include a comprehensive package of preventive, diagnostic, and treatment interventions, implemented over six days by health teams and mobile medical clinics. He added that health teams will visit displacement camps to conduct the necessary tests to detect malaria and dengue fever cases and provide treatment to affected individuals. They will also carry out entomological surveys to assess vector density and identify areas where disease vectors are prevalent, helping direct interventions according to the actual needs of each area.
    The project is part of Saudi Arabia's ongoing humanitarian and health efforts through KSrelief to strengthen health prevention measures, protect the Yemeni people from epidemic diseases, and improve their health and living conditions amid the ongoing humanitarian crisis.
    -- SPA
